title: 6.23.2 Sub-build: One die, two turns
description: One die, two names, one turn index. Roll and pass before there is a board.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: It says Red's turn and the last roll is 0. SPACE does nothing yet.

steps.title: Roll the die
steps.instructions: Inside `if (kb.presses('space'))`, set `roll = floor(random(1, 7));`. Press SPACE a few times: every number from 1 to 6 turns up, and never a 0 or a 7.

steps.title: Pass the turn
steps.instructions: On the line after the roll, pass the turn: `turn = (turn + 1) % 2;`. Each SPACE should now switch between Red and Blue.
hints: `%` is the remainder: `2 % 2` is 0, so after Blue it is Red again.
Put it inside the same `if`, or the turn flips every frame.

steps.title: A fresh start each Run
steps.instructions: Press Run three times and write down the first three rolls: they are the same every time. In `setup()`, add `randomSeed(Date.now());` and try again. Now each Run rolls differently.
hints: `Date.now()` is the time in thousandths of a second, so it changes on every Run.

requirements.title: A roll from 1 to 6
requirements.description: A whole number from 1 to 6, as floor(random(1, 7)) gives. Help: 6.23.1 (Reading: A die, and whose turn it is)

requirements.title: The turn passes
requirements.description: The turn moves to the other player, with % or another way that goes back to 0. Help: 6.23.1 (Reading: A die, and whose turn it is)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: One die, two turns". The task: on SPACE, roll a whole number from 1 to 6 and pass the turn to the other player so it goes back to the first after the last. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: The turn passes
rubric.description: Each roll moves the turn on and wraps back to 0.
